findings.claim: Linear coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of unmodified Yixing Zisha subtypes (Zini, Hongni, Dicaoqing, Zhuni) in open peer-reviewed literature
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: No open peer-reviewed measurements of linear CTE resolved by Yixing subtype (Zini, Hongni, Dicaoqing, Zhuni) were found in Ceramics International, MDPI, Journal of Ceramic Science and Technology, Scientific Reports, or Chinese ceramic engineering journals searched. Wu et al. (2013) use dilatometry/thermal-expansion inflection to reconstruct historical firing temperatures rather than publishing subtype CTE tables. Unattributed blogs circulate 4.5-6.5 x 10^-6 /°C, which lack primary verification.
sources: Wu et al. (2013), Ceramics International, DOI: 10.1016/j.ceramint.2012.09.021
findings.value_or_range: Unmeasured / unpublished by subtype in open peer-reviewed literature and omitted from GB/T 10816

findings.claim: Specific heat capacity (Cp) and thermal diffusivity (alpha) of Yixing Zisha subtypes (Zini, Hongni, Dicaoqing, Zhuni)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: No direct open peer-reviewed DSC (Cp) or laser-flash (thermal diffusivity) measurements resolved by Yixing Zisha clay subtype were found. Generic ceramic/clay values (~0.75-1.0 J/(g·K), e.g., 0.92 kJ/(kg·K)) cited on tea blogs lack primary experimental attribution to Yixing Zisha.
sources: Yang et al. (2021), Ceramics International, DOI: 10.1016/j.ceramint.2020.12.178
findings.value_or_range: Unmeasured / unpublished by subtype in open primary peer-reviewed literature

findings.claim: Thermal conductivity (k) of Zisha ceramic used in thermodynamic modeling of a Zisha jetting thermometer
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Single-source peer-reviewed parameter; clay subtype (e.g., Zini vs. Zhuni) and porosity variation are not resolved across subtypes. Wider ranges (0.15-1.8 W/(m·K)) appear in non-primary secondary sites without peer-reviewed traceability.
sources: Lee & Attinger (2016), Scientific Reports 6:28609, DOI: 10.1038/srep28609 (NIH PMC / CrossRef)

findings.claim: Natural fired Zisha mineralogy relies on quartz, mullite, hematite, amorphous glassy phase, and minor cristobalite rather than lithium or cordierite flameware minerals
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Confirmed across multiple independent peer-reviewed XRD/microstructural studies: raw clays (kaolinite, illite/muscovite, quartz, hematite/goethite) transform upon firing into quartz + mullite + hematite + amorphous glass (+ minor cristobalite), with zero natural spodumene, petalite, or cordierite.
sources: Wu et al. (2013), Ceramics International, DOI: 10.1016/j.ceramint.2012.09.021
Yang et al. (2021), Ceramics International, DOI: 10.1016/j.ceramint.2020.12.178
Lin et al. (2021), J. Ceram. Sci. Technol., DOI: 10.4416/JCST2021-00004
MDPI Foods Baijiu-aging Zisha sintering study (1200 °C)
findings.value_or_range: Quartz + mullite + hematite + amorphous phase (+ minor cristobalite); no natural lithium/cordierite phases

findings.claim: Quantitative fired phase assemblage of Dicaoqing-Zisha fired at 1180 °C
findings.confidence: LOW CONFIDENCE (single peer-reviewed source for exact wt%)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Exact wt% breakdown is from a single peer-reviewed Ceramics International study; phase identity is corroborated across multiple studies.
sources: Yang et al. (2021), Ceramics International, DOI: 10.1016/j.ceramint.2020.12.178
findings.value_or_range: Quartz 33.2, Mullite 32.8, Amorphous phase 24.9, Hematite 5.9, Cristobalite 3.2

findings.claim: Quantitative fired phase assemblage of Benshanzhu-Zisha (Zhuni/Hongni family)
findings.confidence: LOW CONFIDENCE (single peer-reviewed source for exact wt%)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Exact wt% values are from a single peer-reviewed study; shows higher Fe2O3/hematite fluxing produces a much larger amorphous glassy matrix and lower mullite than Dicaoqing.
findings.value_or_range: Amorphous phase 71.2, Hematite 11.5, Mullite 10.7 (balance residual quartz/other)

findings.claim: Low-expansion lithium-silicate/cordierite phases in Zisha occur only in engineered flameware formulations via deliberate additives
findings.confidence: LOW CONFIDENCE (single-source quantitative CTE 1.32; HIGH CONFIDENCE on additive mechanism)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: He et al. (2025) used Hainan Zijin purple clay (32.8%) doped with 32.8% spodumene, 9.4% lithium aluminosilicate (锂白石), 10.0% calcined talc, and 15.0% kaolin fired at 1150 °C (60 min) to achieve 1.32 x 10^-6 °C^-1 CTE, 0.25% water absorption, and 83.89 MPa flexural strength—demonstrating that unmodified Zisha lacks lithium/cordierite low-expansion mineralogy.
sources: He et al. (2025), China Ceramics (中国陶瓷), Aug 2025 (researching.cn)

findings.claim: Typical firing/sintering temperature window and intermediate vitrification porosity of Yixing Zisha stoneware
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Zisha is sintered to an intermediate stoneware state with an open/closed dual-pore network rather than zero-porosity porcelain (<0.2-0.5% water absorption). Exact firing temperatures vary by ore body (e.g., Dicaoqing 1180 °C; Baijiu Zisha 1200 °C; historical Shushan wares 1100-1180 °C).
sources: Wu et al. (2013), Ceramics International, DOI: 10.1016/j.ceramint.2012.09.021
Yang et al. (2021), Ceramics International, DOI: 10.1016/j.ceramint.2020.12.178
findings.value_or_range: 1100-1200 °C firing; ~8-11% apparent porosity in Ming/Qing shards

findings.claim: GB/T 10816 national standard requirements for Zisha pottery thermal shock resistance and water absorption
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: GB/T 10816-2008 required 2.5%-6.0% water absorption (pots/cups/plates/steam pots; <=12.0% flowerpots) and 200 °C to 20 °C single water-quench without cracking. GB/T 10816-2024 (effective 2025-07-01) consolidated water absorption to <=6.0% (excluding flowerpots) and revised thermal shock to 180 °C to 20 °C single water-quench without cracking (plus microwave/oven-freezer transition tests). Neither edition specifies CTE, Cp, or thermal diffusivity limits.
findings.value_or_range: Water absorption <=6.0% (2.5-6.0% in 2008); thermal shock 180 °C -> 20 °C (200 °C -> 20 °C in 2008)

myths_checked: MYTH: Yixing Zisha relies on lithium aluminosilicate (spodumene, petalite) or cordierite flameware minerals for thermal shock resistance. VERDICT: FALSE — peer-reviewed XRD shows natural fired Zisha relies on quartz, mullite, hematite, and an amorphous phase with a dual-pore, unglazed body; spodumene/petalite/cordierite appear only in deliberately doped modern cookware formulations.

MYTH: GB/T 10816 specifies numerical CTE, specific heat capacity, or thermal diffusivity thresholds for Yixing Zisha. VERDICT: FALSE — GB/T 10816-2008 and GB/T 10816-2024 regulate performance-based thermal shock quenching (200->20 °C in 2008; 180->20 °C in 2024) and water absorption (2.5-6.0% in 2008; <=6.0% in 2024), not CTE/Cp/diffusivity.

MYTH: Subtype-specific linear CTEs (e.g., 4.5-4.8 x 10^-6 /°C for Zini vs. 5.0-6.5 x 10^-6 /°C for Zhuni) and Cp (0.92 kJ/kg·K) are established in peer-reviewed ceramic engineering literature or DB32/T 3651-2019. VERDICT: UNVERIFIED / MISATTRIBUTED — those figures circulate on unattributed blogs (jianshu.com, baidu.com) without traceable peer-reviewed measurement, and DB32/T 3651-2019 is actually a Jiangsu peach grading standard rather than a Zisha clay standard.

MYTH: Yixing Zisha fires to full, non-porous porcelain vitrification. VERDICT: FALSE — Zisha is fired at ~1100-1200 °C to an intermediate stoneware state retaining an open/closed dual-pore network (~8-11% apparent porosity in historical shards; <=6.0% water absorption limit under GB/T 10816).
